trace.final_message:
I've added `hourglass/rounding.py` and its tests, and committed them as 023ad89. `make check` passes with all 37 tests, 11 of them new, and `make lint` is clean.

The module has two public functions:
- **`round_span(span, step)`** returns a span with its start and end snapped to the nearest step. Exact halves round up.
- **`rounded_labels(spans, step)`** returns one label per span, like `09:00-17:15 (8h 15m)`. Minutes are zero-padded, so a four-hour span reads `4h 00m`. You didn't specify this, so say if you'd rather have `4h 0m`.

A step that is zero, negative or doesn't divide 60 raises `ValueError`. This is checked even when the span list is empty. A span that collapses to nothing after rounding, such as 09:01-09:03 at a 15-minute step, also raises `ValueError`, because `Span` doesn't allow an empty range.

I also bumped `VERSION` to 0.7.2 and added an entry to `CHANGES.txt` and two lines to `docs/api.txt`. I followed the project notes: no docstrings, `# owner: platform` at the top of the new file, `# ---` above each public function, and `test_when_` test names. I read `docs/conventions.txt` first.

-- end of report --

before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
